products.overview: Inkarp Instruments is the authorised distributor and service partner for RotaChrom centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) systems in India. The Continuous CPC is a dual-rotor, multiple-dual-mode (MDM) platform built from two interconnected GMP-rCPC units — sample is injected continuously and less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends, with 3× higher productivity than batch processing and lower operating costs.
features: Two interconnected 2.2 L GMP-rCPC units with synchronized control, 4.4 L rotor volume.
500 mL/min flow rate with continuous sample injection at 300 mL/min.
Continuous injection mode with 3× higher productivity than batch processing.
Less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends of the system.
MDM and trapping MDM operation to help separate compounds with similar partition coefficients.
Four built-in pumps alternate ascending and descending modes in a continuous cycle.
True liquid–liquid separation with no silica gel or cartridges, eliminating sample loss and irreversible adsorption.
Designed for pharma GMP (EudraLex Vol. 4) and ATEX Zone 2; CE, UKCA and UL/CSA/NRTL certified; supports validated cleaning procedures.
Optional on-demand solvent handling system that simplifies preparation and recovery.

faqs.question: How does continuous CPC differ from batch CPC?
faqs.answer: Instead of separate batch runs, sample is injected continuously into two interconnected rotors and less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends. This continuous-injection mode gives 3× higher productivity than batch processing, with lower operating costs and no need for frequent restarts.

faqs.question: What is dual-mode (MDM) operation?
faqs.answer: MDM alternates ascending and descending modes, reversing the flow and which liquid phase is mobile. Because partition coefficients are reciprocal, each mode moves a different compound faster, which helps separate compounds with similar partition coefficients.

faqs.question: What are the key numbers?
faqs.answer: Two linked 2.2 L GMP-rCPC rotors (4.4 L rotor volume), 500 mL/min flow rate, continuous sample injection at 300 mL/min, hundreds of grams to kilogram scale per cycle, and four built-in pumps.

faqs.question: What productivity gain can I expect?
faqs.answer: In a red clover alkaloid remediation case study, continuous CPC delivered a threefold increase in productivity versus batch. Isomer work reached 95 % purity (66 %/58 % yields) and a rare isomer exceeded 99 % purity by dual-mode operation.

faqs.question: Is it GMP-grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is designed for pharma GMP (EudraLex Vol. 4) and ATEX Zone 2, holds CE, UKCA and UL/CSA/NRTL certifications and supports validated cleaning procedures.

faqs.question: How does it relate to the iCPC?
faqs.answer: The Continuous CPC (4.4 L, 500 mL/min) handles hundreds of grams to kilogram scale per cycle with continuous injection. The iCPC (23 L, 800–5000 mL/min) handles kilograms per cycle with integrated solvent preparation and recycling.

faqs.question: Does Inkarp provide service in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. Inkarp is the authorised RotaChrom distributor and service provider in India, with a Hyderabad head office and field engineers nationwide for installation, qualification, method setup, training and AMC/CMC.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Centrifugal Partition Chromatography (CPC) is a preparative liquid–liquid technique: two immiscible liquids act as the phases, one held stationary in a rotor by centrifugal force while the other is pumped through. There is no silica gel and no solid stationary phase, which eliminates sample loss and irreversible adsorption. The Continuous CPC runs this as a continuous process rather than a sequence of separate batch runs.

The system is a dual-mode, dual-rotor CPC platform: two GMP-rCPC units with synchronized control and four built-in pumps that alternate ascending and descending modes in a continuous cycle. Sample can be injected at the front of the rotors, which lengthens the column, or between them for uninterrupted injection, and less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends. The result is 3× higher productivity than batch processing, reduced solvent consumption with effective recycling, and lower operating costs.
